channel.title: Cagri Temel
channel.description: Notes on explainable AI, AI safety, Chain-of-Thought reasoning, and building trustworthy AI products.

item.title: The Robot Ran 100 Metres Faster Than Bolt. Then It Hit the Barrier.
item.description: Tiangong Ultra ran 100 metres in 8.64 seconds in Beijing and several finishers crashed into a padded barrier. Why stopping is the harder half, and why the binding limit changes from geometry to friction the moment the robot leaves the track.

item.title: The Signal Was There. It Was Eight Seconds Late.
item.description: A terrain classifier that had to answer while the robot was still on the slippery patch. The information was in the data, but the decision arrived 8.3 seconds into a crossing that takes about ten.

item.title: I Reviewed for Five Conferences This Year. The Same Paper Keeps Arriving.
item.description: Most submissions I score low are not wrong, they are unfalsifiable by the reader. Why correct ablations are blind to a fault in the substrate every arm shares, and the five questions I ask instead.

item.title: My Robot Was Tipping 13 Degrees. That Was the Whole Result.
item.description: A wheel-slip study invalidated by its own apparatus. Why four months of correct ablations could not catch it, and how slip was re-established on a controlled ramp.

item.title: My Slip Detector Was Accurate. It Was Also Useless.
item.description: A slip detector scored 0.869 accuracy and cut position error by 72 percent. The control arm, driving slower with no detector at all, did better.

item.title: Welcome: what I write about
item.description: Why I started this blog and the topics I will cover: trustworthy AI, explainable reasoning, and lessons from building real AI products.
